5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Past simple: irregular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Recognise irregular verbs (verbos irregulares) in a text
  • Learn the 30 most common irregular past forms
  • Use irregular verbs in affirmative, negative and question sentences
  • Tell a short story in the past
  • Know the three forms of irregular verbs and how to check them
  • Use irregular verbs to retell fairy tales and talk about the weekend
  • Choose between was/were and did

Para pensar

Si «jugué» es played, ¿por qué «fui» no es goed?

Explicación

1. What is an irregular verb?

Regular verbs add -ed: play → played. Irregular verbs don't follow this rule. Each one has its own past form: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had.

The good news: like regular verbs, the past form is the same for all persons: «I went», «she went», «they went». And irregular verbs are very common, so you hear them all the time in songs, films and stories. En castellano: nosotros también tenemos irregulares: «ir» → «fui», no «í». En inglés es igual: hay que memorizarlos.

2. The top ten

Start with the ten most useful irregular verbs. You will use them every day: go → went (ir), have → had (tener), get → got (conseguir, llegar), make → made (hacer, fabricar), do → did (hacer), see → saw (ver), come → came (venir), eat → ate (comer), take → took (coger, llevar), say → said (decir).

«I went to the park and I saw my friends. We had a picnic and we ate sandwiches. Then Marc came with his dog and said hello.»

3. Learn them in families

Many irregular verbs change in a similar way. Learn them in families. i → a: swim → swam, sing → sang, drink → drank, begin → began, ring → rang. -ought / -aught: buy → bought, bring → brought, think → thought, catch → caught, teach → taught.

ee → e / ea → e: sleep → slept, feel → felt, meet → met, keep → kept. o-e: write → wrote, ride → rode, drive → drove. Same form: put → put, cut → cut, hit → hit, let → let. Consejo: agrupados se recuerdan mucho mejor que en una lista por orden alfabético.

4. More useful verbs

Here are more irregular verbs for your stories: run → ran, sit → sat, stand → stood, fall → fell, find → found, lose → lost, win → won, give → gave, tell → told, read → read (it is written the same but sounds «red»), wear → wore, fly → flew, know → knew, leave → left, break → broke.

«The bird flew away.» «Our team won the match!» «I lost my keys, but my brother found them under the sofa.» «Grandpa told us a story.»

5. The three forms of a verb

In dictionaries and in lists of irregular verbs you will find three columns. Now you only need the first two, but it's good to know what the third one is:

  1. Base form (infinitive): the verb in the dictionary. go, eat, see.
  2. Past simple: the form for finished actions. went, ate, saw.
  3. Past participle: used in other tenses that you will learn in the next years (like the present perfect: «I have eaten»). gone, eaten, seen.

In regular verbs, the past simple and the past participle are the same: play – played – played. In irregular verbs there are different patterns:

  • A – A – A: the three forms are the same: put – put – put, cut – cut – cut.
  • A – B – B: the second and third are the same: buy – bought – bought, sleep – slept – slept.
  • A – B – C: the three forms are different: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten.
  • A – B – A: the first and third are the same: come – came – come, run – ran – run.

When you learn a new irregular verb, say the three forms aloud like a song: «go, went, gone; see, saw, seen».

6. Negatives: didn't + base form

The negative works exactly like with regular verbs: didn't + the base form (the verb as in the dictionary). «I didn't go to the party.» «She didn't eat her vegetables.» «We didn't see the eclipse.»

This is a big help: in negatives you don't need the irregular form. Not «I didn't went», not «She didn't ate». En castellano: piensa que did ya «lleva» el pasado; el verbo vuelve a ser el de siempre. Solo tienes que acordarte del irregular en las frases afirmativas.

7. Questions: Did…? Where did…?

Questions also use did + subject + base form: «Did you see the fireworks?» «Yes, I did.» «Did he take the bus?» «No, he didn't. He walked.»

With question words: «Where did you go on holiday?» «What did you eat?» «Who did you meet?» «What time did the train leave?» The answer uses the irregular past: «I went to Galicia.» «I ate octopus.» «I met my cousins.»

8. Regular or irregular? How to check

How do you know if a verb is regular or irregular? Unfortunately, there is no rule: you can't see it in the verb. But there are some good strategies:

  • Look at a list: most English books have a list of irregular verbs at the end. Keep a copy in your notebook.
  • Use a dictionary: in a good dictionary, irregular verbs show their past forms next to the word: «swim (swam, swum)». If you don't see any forms, the verb is regular.
  • Think of the most common verbs: the most frequent verbs in English (be, have, do, go, get, make, see, come, take, say) are almost all irregular. New verbs (like text, google, download) are always regular.
  • Be careful with similar verbs: look is regular (looked) but see is irregular (saw); listen is regular (listened) but hear is irregular (heard); stay is regular but stand is irregular (stood).

Good news: in questions and negatives with did, you always use the base form, so you don't need the irregular form! «Did you see it? No, I didn't see it.»

9. Tricks to remember them

1. Flashcards: write the verb on one side and the past on the other. Practise five every day. 2. Rhythm: say them with a beat, clapping: «go – went, see – saw, eat – ate!». 3. Memory game: place the cards face down and find the pairs.

4. Your own sentences: use each new verb in a true sentence about you: «Last summer I swam in the sea.» 5. Read stories: stories in the past are full of irregular verbs. Consejo: no intentes aprender cien de golpe. Con los treinta de este tema ya puedes contar casi cualquier cosa.

10. Irregular verbs in fairy tales

Fairy tales are full of irregular verbs, because they tell stories in the past. Read this short version of Little Red Riding Hood (Caperucita Roja):

«Once upon a time there was a girl who wore a red hood. One day, her mother gave her a basket of food for her grandmother. The girl went into the forest. There she met a wolf. The wolf ran to Grandma's house, ate her and put on her clothes. When the girl came, she said: "Grandma, what big eyes you have!" Suddenly, a hunter heard a noise. He found the wolf, took Grandma out and they all lived happily ever after.»

Fairy tales have typical expressions that you can use in your own stories:

  • Once upon a time… (Érase una vez…)
  • One day… (Un día…)
  • Suddenly… (De repente…)
  • In the end… (Al final…)
  • …and they lived happily ever after. (…y vivieron felices para siempre.)

Choose another tale you know (Cinderella, The Three Little Pigs, Snow White) and retell it in English using irregular verbs.

11. Reading: the lost dog

Read this story: «Last Sunday, Max woke up early and took his dog Coco to the park. Coco saw a squirrel and ran after it. Max called her, but she didn't come back. Max felt very worried. He looked everywhere and asked people. An old lady said: "I saw a small dog near the fountain." Max went there and he found Coco. She was wet and happy! They had an ice cream and came home.»

Underline the irregular verbs in red and the regular ones in blue. What did Coco see? Where did Max find her?

12. Let's practise: chain story

Play a chain story in groups of four. The first person says a sentence with an irregular verb: «Yesterday a dragon came to our school.» The next person continues: «It ate all the sandwiches.» «Then it flew to the gym.» «Finally it fell asleep in the library!»

Write your story and draw it in four pictures. Check each verb: is it regular or irregular? Did you use the base form after didn't? Repaso: afirmativa con la forma irregular; negativa y pregunta con did + verbo básico.

13. Was / were or did?

Many students mix was/were and did. Here is the key:

  • With the verb to be (ser, estar), use was / were. Don't use did: «I was tired.» → «I wasn't tired.» → «Were you tired?»
  • With all other verbs, use the past form in affirmative sentences, and did / didn't in negatives and questions: «I slept well.» → «I didn't sleep well.» → «Did you sleep well?»

Look at the mistakes and the correct sentences:

  • «I didn't was at home.» ✗ → «I wasn't at home.» ✓
  • «Did you were happy?» ✗ → «Were you happy?» ✓
  • «Was you go to the cinema?» ✗ → «Did you go to the cinema?» ✓
  • «She wasn't eat.» ✗ → «She didn't eat.» ✓

A trick: look for the main verb. If it is be (with an adjective or a place after it: tired, happy, at home), use was/were. If there is another verb (go, eat, sleep), use did.

Both can appear together: «I was hungry, so I ate a sandwich. I didn't eat a pizza because there wasn't any.»

14. Talking about your weekend

On Monday mornings, English teachers often ask: «What did you do at the weekend?» Here are some useful frames to answer well, with irregular verbs:

  • Where: «I went to the beach / to my grandparents' house / to the cinema.»
  • Who: «I met my cousins.» «I saw my friends.»
  • Food: «We had lunch in a restaurant. I ate spaghetti and I drank orange juice.»
  • Activities: «I rode my bike.» «I swam in the pool.» «I read a comic.» «We made a cake.»
  • Feelings: «It was fun / boring / amazing.» «I felt tired but happy.»

Don't just say «I went to the park». Give details: when, who, what you did and how it was. «On Saturday afternoon I went to the park with my sister. We flew a kite and we ran a lot. It was windy and great fun!»

Then ask back: «And you? What did you do?» A conversation is like a tennis match: the ball must go and come back.

Irregular verbs

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: go, have, see, make.

  2. Write the past: sing, drink, think, catch.

  3. Complete: «Yesterday I ___ (eat) paella.»

  4. Complete: «My aunt ___ (give) me a book.»

  5. Make it negative: «We took a taxi.»

  6. Make a question: «She wrote a poem.»

  7. Ask with what: «He bought a skateboard.»

  8. Correct: «I didn't saw the match, but my team winned.»

  9. Which family? «keep → kept»

  10. Write four sentences about your best day with irregular verbs.

  11. Write the past: give, come, wear, meet, hear.

  12. Is it regular or irregular? look, see, listen, hear.

  13. Translate: «Érase una vez…» and «De repente…».

  14. Answer: «What did you do at the weekend?» (two sentences)

  15. Complete: «I ___ tired, so I ___ to bed early.» (be, go)

  16. Write the three forms of: go, see, come.

  17. Correct: «Did you were at the party?» and «I didn't was hungry.»

  18. Find the regular verb in the reading «The best day of the year».

  19. Write the questions: «I ate pizza.» (What) / «We went to Madrid.» (Where)

  20. Classify by pattern: cut, sleep, eat, run.

  21. Retell The Three Little Pigs in eight sentences with irregular verbs.

  22. Write about your best day of the year with at least ten irregular verbs.

  23. Write a dialogue about the weekend with a partner: four questions and four answers.

  24. Explain in Spanish when we use was/were and when we use did.

Practica

  1. The past of «go» is…

    1. A) goed
    2. B) gone
    3. C) went

  2. The past of «eat» is…

    1. A) ate
    2. B) eated
    3. C) eat

  3. The past of «buy» is…

    1. A) buyed
    2. B) bought
    3. C) brought

  4. The past of «swim» is…

    1. A) swimmed
    2. B) swam
    3. C) swum

  5. «I didn't ___ the film.»

    1. A) saw
    2. B) seen
    3. C) see

  6. «Did you ___ a good time?»

    1. A) have
    2. B) had
    3. C) has

  7. The past of «put» is…

    1. A) putted
    2. B) pat
    3. C) put

  8. «Where did they go?» — «They ___ to Paris.»

    1. A) go
    2. B) went
    3. C) did go

  9. The past of «sleep» is…

    1. A) slept
    2. B) sleeped
    3. C) slep

  10. Which verb is irregular?

    1. A) write
    2. B) walk
    3. C) play

  11. The three forms of «go» are…

    1. A) go – goed – gone
    2. B) go – went – gone
    3. C) go – went – went

  12. «Once upon a time» means…

    1. A) De repente
    2. B) Al final
    3. C) Érase una vez

  13. «___ you happy?»

    1. A) Did
    2. B) Were
    3. C) Was

  14. «She ___ eat the cake.»

    1. A) didn't
    2. B) wasn't
    3. C) weren't

  15. Which verb is regular?

    1. A) drink
    2. B) draw
    3. C) download

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué diferencia hay entre un verbo regular y uno irregular; Cuáles son los diez irregulares más usados y su pasado; Por qué en negativas y preguntas no se usa la forma irregular; Qué trucos ayudan a memorizarlos.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

go → wentir → fui.
have → hadtener → tuve.
see → sawver → vi.
eat → atecomer → comí.
buy → boughtcomprar (familia -ought).
swim → swamnadar (familia i → a).
put → putIgual en presente y pasado.
didn't + base formI didn't go (no «didn't went»).
Three formsbase – past – participle: see – saw – seen.
How to checkIrregular verbs list or dictionary.
Fairy talesOnce upon a time… happily ever after.
was/were vs didbe → was/were; other verbs → did.

Soluciones

  1. C) Irregular.
  2. A) Irregular.
  3. B) Familia -ought.
  4. B) i → a.
  5. C) Tras didn't, forma básica.
  6. A) Tras did, forma básica.
  7. C) Igual que el presente.
  8. B) Respuesta en afirmativa: went.
  9. A) ee → e.
  10. A) write → wrote.
  11. B) A–B–C.
  12. C) Typical start of tales.
  13. B) To be with you.
  14. A) Eat → did.
  15. C) New verbs are regular.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. went, had, saw, made.
  2. sang, drank, thought, caught.
  3. ate.
  4. gave.
  5. We didn't take a taxi.
  6. Did she write a poem?
  7. What did he buy?
  8. I didn't see the match, but my team won.
  9. ee → e, como sleep → slept y feel → felt.
  10. Model answer: I went to the beach. I swam in the sea. We had lunch in a restaurant. I felt very happy.
  11. gave, came, wore, met, heard.
  12. look and listen are regular; see and hear are irregular.
  13. Once upon a time… / Suddenly…
  14. Open answer. Example: I went to the park. I rode my bike.
  15. was, went.
  16. go–went–gone; see–saw–seen; come–came–come.
  17. Were you at the party? I wasn't hungry.
  18. clapped.
  19. What did you eat? Where did you go?
  20. cut A–A–A; sleep A–B–B; eat A–B–C; run A–B–A.
  21. Open answer. Example: The wolf came… he blew the house down…
  22. Open answer.
  23. Open answer with did, was/were and irregular verbs.
  24. Was/were con el verbo to be; did en negativas y preguntas con los demás verbos.
